item.title: Statement from Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson on Wrongful Detention Designation for U.S. Citizen Min Zin
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Statement from Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson on Wrongful Detention Designation for U.S. Citizen Min Zin

Media Note

August 20, 2026

Secretary Rubio has determined that U.S. citizen Min Zin is wrongfully detained in China. This follows an extensive review of the circumstances surrounding his June 3 detention in Yunnan, China, where Mr. Zin had traveled to attend an academic conference at the invitation of the Chinese government. There are now two wrongfully detained U.S. citizens in China: Mr. Zin and Dr. Youlin Chen.

The safety and security of U.S. citizens is the State Department’s top priority. We will continue to advocate for Mr. Zin and call for the release of all U.S. citizens who are arbitrarily detained or exit banned in China.

item.title: Hungary National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Hungary National Day

Press Statement

August 20, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I send my warmest wishes to the people of Hungary as you celebrate your National Day.

As Hungary commemorates St. Stephen’s Day and the founding of your nation, we are reminded of the historic ties between our peoples.  The friendship between the United States and Hungary rests on the foundation of a mutual respect for sovereignty, proud heritage, and the hard-won liberties that define our two republics.

Today, the United States reaffirms its strong and forward-looking partnership with Hungary, one sustained by deep economic ties, shared security interests, and a commitment to the values that have long united the West.

May the bonds between the United States and Hungary continue to allow both our nations to prosper.

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Norwegian State Secretary Kravik

Readout

August 19, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Thomas Pigott:

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met with Norwegian State Secretary Andreas Motzfeldt Kravik today to discuss areas of mutual interest.  The Deputy Secretary and State Secretary discussed common interests in promoting peace in the Middle East and deepening cooperation on security in Europe, among other issues.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with UAE National Security Advisor Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio’s Call with UAE National Security Advisor Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan

Readout

August 18, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott:

Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with UAE National Security Advisor Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The two discussed a number of regional security issues, including Lebanon, as well as continued U.S.-UAE coordination to hold Iran and its terrorist proxies accountable for ongoing attacks. Secretary Rubio underscored the importance of freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with Colombian President de la Espriella
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio’s Call with Colombian President de la Espriella 

Readout

August 18, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott: 

Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with President Abelardo de la Espriella today to discuss ongoing U.S. support to the people of Colombia following the devastating August 10 earthquake.  The United States has provided $26.5 million in emergency humanitarian assistance, deployed search and rescue teams, and provided C-130 airlift flights to help Colombia’s recovery.

item.title: Advancing the United States’ Campaign to Address the Threat Posed by the International Criminal Court
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Advancing the United States’ Campaign to Address the Threat Posed by the International Criminal Court 

Press Statement

August 18, 2026

The Trump Administration has been clear: the International Criminal Court (ICC) is a corrupt and fatally politicized supranational court that has maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate.  We will not tolerate its assault on state sovereignty.  

In furtherance of the diplomatic campaign we launched last month to address the ICC’s abuses of power, I am designating two ICC officials – President of the ICC, Tomoko Akane of Japan, and ICC Senior Trial Lawyer, Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal – pursuant to Executive Order 14203, “Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court.”  These individuals have directly engaged in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government has not consented to ICC jurisdiction.  

The ICC has repeatedly attempted to assert authority over nationals of the United States and other countries that have not consented to its jurisdiction or ratified the Rome Statute.  This sets a dangerous precedent for all nations.   

Our whole of government campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the ICC to national sovereignty will be sweeping and we expect more countries to join our campaign by ending their funding and participation in this politicized and unaccountable court. The ICC’s ability to target American nationals and those of other non-States Parties must end. The Trump Administration stands ready to take additional measures, if necessary, to systematically dismantle the ICC until it is incapable of threatening American sovereignty. 

These individuals are being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order (E.O.) 14203.

item.title: The Gabonese Republic National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

The Gabonese Republic National Day

Press Statement

August 16, 2026

On behalf of the United States, I am pleased to extend warm congratulations to the people of Gabon as you celebrate the 66th anniversary of your independence on August 17.

Our growing commercial ties and deepening security cooperation reflect a shared commitment to a stable, prosperous, and sovereign Gabon.

As Gabon looks toward its future, the United States stands as a steadfast partner. We wish the Gabonese people health, peace, and continued prosperity in the year ahead.

item.title: Indonesia Independence Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Indonesia Independence Day

Press Statement

August 16, 2026

On behalf of the people of the United States of America, I extend my warmest congratulations on the 81st anniversary of Indonesia’s independence.

The United States and Indonesia enjoy an enduring partnership rooted in dedication to democratic governance and a shared vision for a free and open Indo-Pacific. Our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership reflects the depth of our cooperation – from defense and regional security to fair and balanced trade, energy, and technology. The United States looks forward to creating new avenues of opportunity for our nations in priority areas such as critical minerals, maritime security, and the digital economy. We offer our heartfelt congratulations to you and the people of Indonesia as we continue our journey together toward shared prosperity.

We also extend deepest condolences to those who lost loved ones in the devastating earthquake and its aftermath in East Nusa Tenggara. Our thoughts are with those who were injured and all communities affected by this tragedy.

item.title: Liechtenstein National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Liechtenstein National Day

Press Statement

August 15, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Liechtenstein on your National Day.

The United States maintains a long-standing partnership with Liechtenstein, grounded in a commitment to freedom and cooperation on business and investment. We continue to work together to advance our mutual prosperity and commercial diplomacy goals.

As we look to the year ahead, we remain dedicated to deepening our commercial ties and fostering the innovation and prosperity that benefit both our peoples. On this National Day, I extend my best wishes to the people of Liechtenstein.

item.title: The Republic of the Congo National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

The Republic of the Congo National Day

Press Statement

August 15, 2026

On behalf of the United States, I extend our congratulations to the people of the Republic of the Congo on the 66th anniversary of its independence.

We are proud of our historic collaboration, which began over six decades ago when the United States recognized the Republic of the Congo on the day of its independence. I look forward to furthering our partnership by strengthening our countries’ commercial and security relationship for the welfare of our citizens.

The United States wishes the Republic of the Congo a prosperous year ahead.
